businessType: Investor-owned regional electric utility (regulated). ~$3B annual revenue, ~1.6M retail customers across a multi-county service territory. Vertically integrated: generation, transmission, and distribution. Revenue is set by the state Public Utility Commission (PUC) through periodic rate cases that establish an allowed rate of return on a regulatory-approved rate base. Public company (NYSE-listed parent). ~4,800 employees.
stage: FY2025: Revenue $3,000M (up 2.4% from $2,930M FY2024, within PUC-allowed 2-3% rate growth band). Rate base $9,000M FY2025, planned to grow to ~$10,200M (+13%) over the multi-year capital plan horizon. Allowed ROE 9.8% (set in last rate case); earned/realized ROE 8.2% FY2025, down from 9.5% FY2023 (~160 bps of under-earning vs allowed). Annual capex $1,100M vs depreciation ~$650M (capex/depreciation 1.69x). EBITDA stable. Equity ~50% of rate base (~$4,500M). Investment-grade credit rating, but rating agencies flagging persistent under-earning.
ownerGoal: Close the gap between earned ROE (8.2%) and allowed ROE (9.8%) and restore the realized return toward the allowed level, while continuing to fund the mandated capital plan (grid hardening, reliability, decarbonization). Sustain the investment-grade credit rating and maintain constructive regulatory and political relationships. Decide, before the next rate-case filing window, how to structure the next filing to stop locking in multi-year under-earning.
ownerConstraints: Pricing constraint: Rates are set by the state PUC, not by management. The utility cannot self-price or unilaterally raise customer rates; any rate change requires a formal rate-case proceeding and Commission approval.

Return constraint: The allowed ROE (9.8%) is fixed until the next rate case is decided; the utility earns the realized return its rates and costs produce, not the allowed return, and cannot administratively true itself up between cases.

Capital mandate constraint: The capital plan ($1,100M/yr — grid hardening, reliability, safety, decarbonization) is largely mandated by reliability standards, safety obligations, and state decarbonization policy; it cannot simply be cut to protect short-term ROE.

Regulatory lag constraint: Rate cases are filed roughly every ~3 years using a historical test year; current rates reflect a test year ~24 months old, so approved revenue chronically trails the actual cost of capital deployed.

Political / affordability constraint: Rate increases face political and consumer-advocate scrutiny on customer affordability; large or frequent rate hikes risk regulatory and political backlash, intervenor opposition, and disallowances.

Compliance constraint: As a regulated entity, the utility must operate within Commission rules, FERC/NERC reliability standards, and state safety codes; recovery mechanisms must be regulator-approved.
immediateConcern: Realized ROE has fallen ~130 bps over two years (9.5% FY2023 to 8.2% FY2025) and now sits ~160 bps below the 9.8% allowed ROE, while the company is deploying $1,100M/yr of capital against only ~$650M of depreciation. Approved revenue is growing 2.4%/yr while the cost of the capital being added is inflating ~9%/yr. Because rates are set on a stale (~24-month-old) test year and only reset every ~3 years, the company is structurally under-recovering its cost of capital between cases. Management must decide before the next rate-case filing window (~120-180 days) whether to file for a forward test year and/or capital cost-recovery trackers/riders; missing the window risks locking in roughly another 3-year cycle of under-earning.
